definition: A training technique that averages model weights collected across multiple points along the training trajectory, typically improving generalization compared to using the final checkpoint alone.
details: SWA leverages the observation that averaging weights from different points in training (particularly with a modified learning rate schedule) often finds flatter, better-generalizing regions of the loss landscape than a single final checkpoint.

explainer.lead: A training technique that averages model weights collected at multiple points along the training trajectory, typically improving generalization over the final checkpoint alone. It matters because it improves generalization at little extra cost.

tiers.eli5: Instead of keeping only the last photo from a trip, you blend several photos taken along the way to get a clearer picture.
tiers.practitioner: Weights are collected across training, often with a modified learning rate schedule, then averaged; the pitfall is that the averaged model is not the raw final checkpoint, so evaluation and export must use the averaged weights.
tiers.paperLevel: Averages weights from different training points rather than using a single final checkpoint; this often finds flatter, better-generalizing regions of the loss landscape.

explainer.example: Collecting weights at several points late in training with a modified learning rate schedule, then averaging them into one model.

citation.title: Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization
